at2.bio: ATM — Andrelita T. Myril — is a painter and visual artist, a graduate of ENARTS, Haiti's most renowned National School of Arts. Her mission: put the tools of art in everyone's hands — to grow each person's creativity, give the mind the escape it needs, and nurture human and mental balance. Her canvases — bold colors, moving rhythms, figures and abstractions — are windows onto the light of Haiti and the Caribbean.

bia.a1_d: Hand the machine what it does well and safely: drafts, summaries, sorting, extraction, translation, file preparation. A task is only delegated once it is understood and measured.
bia.a2_d: Control what it does imperfectly: who validates, at what moment, against which criteria. Every action traced, every output tested — quality becomes provable, not promised.
bia.a3_d: Name the tasks that must stay human — judgement, client relationships, decisions, responsibility — and reinvest the saved time there. That is what makes the project last.
bia.aka: Atmart advisory for companies and NGOs
bia.aka_s: automate · supervise · strengthen the human side
bia.dl1_d: Every task in scope, its volume, its risk, and the decision: delegate, supervise, keep human.
bia.dl2_d: Real cases with the expected answer: you can measure the tool's quality today and again in six months.
bia.dl3_d: A readable log of what the tool did, with which data, and who approved it.
bia.dl4_d: Cost per task and per month, spending caps, and the threshold beyond which automation stops paying off.
bia.dl5_d: What to do when the tool is wrong, breaks down or costs too much — written for your team, not for engineers.
bia.dl6_d: What must never enter an AI tool, who is allowed to approve, and how the people concerned are informed.
bia.dl_d: Deliverables that stay with you and keep working even if you change provider.
bia.end_d: Thirty minutes, no commitment: you describe your work, we tell you where AI can help in your case — and where it should stay out.
bia.eth1: Data literacy. I publish free tutorials — in Haitian Creole, French, English and Spanish — that teach how to read a figure, spot a bias and check a source. Training your teams is part of the job, not an after-sales extra.
bia.eth2: Ethics. A badly defined indicator steers a decision that affects real people. I name the biases, I document the limits, and I refuse conclusions the data does not support — including when they would suit everybody.
bia.eth3: Privacy. Personal data minimised, anonymised, explicit consent. In the recruiting portal I built, a candidate's contact stays hidden until they are selected, and nationality never appears in a browsing list — because the law and human dignity both require it.
bia.fq1_a: That is not the goal, and it is not what we sell. We look for the repetitive tasks that wear your teams out, and we explicitly protect those that require judgement and relationships. An honest diagnostic always states what must NOT be automated.
bia.fq2_a: We sign a confidentiality agreement before any access. The diagnostic sets a written rule on what must never enter an AI tool, and the pilot is designed to work with reduced or anonymised data wherever possible.
bia.fq3_a: That is a real risk and we put it in writing. Every automation ships with its known cost, a spending cap, and a documented manual fallback. You must never be locked in by a provider.
bia.fq3_q: What if the AI provider changes its prices or rules?
bia.fq4_a: Yes — and that is where the effect is strongest: one person recovering five hours a week, in a team of six, is visible. The diagnostic is fixed-price precisely to stay affordable.
bia.fq4_q: We are a small organisation. Is this for us?
bia.fq5_a: Two pilots in parallel, at most. We prefer to say so and keep an honest schedule rather than promise deadlines that quality could not survive.
bia.hw1: A 30-minute call. You describe your work, we say plainly whether AI can help — and if the answer is no, we say that too.
bia.hw2: Diagnostic. Interviews with your teams, observation of the real work, measurement of volumes. No technical decision at this stage.
bia.hw3: Findings workshop. Ninety minutes: the task map, the roadmap, the risks. You decide whether to continue, or you stop there.
bia.hw4: Pilot. A single task, taken through to live use, with your teams in the loop.
bia.hw5: Handover. Your team runs the tool without us. That is the success criterion — not our permanent presence.
bia.kicker: You want to use AI without betting your reputation on it.
bia.lead: Most AI engagements stop at the demo that impresses in a meeting. We don't deliver a demo, we deliver proof: an automation actually in service, traceable, tested, with a known cost — and a clear list of the tasks that must stay human.
bia.lv_d: We always start small: a fixed-price diagnostic, with no obligation to continue.
bia.me2_d: That combination is rare, and it is what makes the difference on an AI project. Most monitoring-and-evaluation specialists do not build the tools they ask for; most developers have never had to defend an indicator in front of a donor. I have done both — which is why I know where automation holds, and where it breaks.
bia.me2_d2: In practice: you will get neither a consultant discovering your sector, nor a developer ignoring your obligations. You will get someone who has filled in the same reports as you, who knows what a donor checks, and who can build the tool the day the analysis says it should be built.
bia.me2_lead: Jean Wisner Myril, founder of Atmart LLC — more than 20 years in the field, four professions that answer each other: monitoring, evaluation & learning · data analysis · data engineering · development.
bia.me_d: The same compass we teach for free on Lojik360 — applied to your organisation, task by task.
bia.me_t: The method: three moves, in this order
bia.n1_l1: Inventory of one team's or one department's tasks
bia.n1_l3: Prioritised roadmap: estimated gain, effort, risk
bia.n1_l4: Risk register: personal data, errors, compliance
bia.n1_l5: A 10 to 15-page report + a 90-minute findings workshop
bia.n2_dur: 4 to 6 weeks · one automation taken all the way
bia.n2_l1: One task from your roadmap, genuinely put into service
bia.n2_l2: Human control designed explicitly: who validates what, and when
bia.n2_l3: Audit trail: every action of the tool is traceable and explainable
bia.n2_l4: A test set that proves quality before and after
bia.n2_l5: Cost model: cost per task, spending caps, predictable budget
bia.n3_l1: One new use case each month
bia.n3_l2: Quality review: tests replayed, drift detected
bia.n3_l3: Career360 Team licences included for your staff
bia.n3_l4: Internal rules and governance kept up to date
bia.of_d: We are opening this practice: the first two organisations get a launch rate in exchange for honest feedback and permission to cite the case (figures anonymised if you prefer). You gain on price, we gain the reference.
bia.pb1_d: The prototype works on three hand-picked examples. At the first unusual case nobody knows what to do, and the team goes back to its old method.
bia.pb1_t: The demo doesn't survive real work
bia.pb2_d: With no record of actions and decisions, you cannot fix an error, answer an audit, or simply trust the thing.
bia.pb2_t: Nobody can say what the tool did
bia.pb3_d: Judgement, relationships, responsibility: automated carelessly, they cost you customers, staff, and sometimes a reputation.
bia.pb_d: Three causes, always the same — and none of them is technical.
bia.pb_t: Why AI projects fail inside companies
bia.pil1_d: Logframes, indicators, field data collection (Kobo, XLSForm), data-quality control against explicit criteria, donor reports. Twenty years producing these documents — and training the teams who fill them in.
bia.pil2_d: Management dashboards (Power BI), quantitative and qualitative analysis. Turning incomplete field data into decisions you can defend in front of a board or a donor.
bia.pil3_d: Cleaning, modelling, de-duplication, documented and reusable datasets — up to complete national geographic reference files, ready for analysis.
bia.pil4_d: Applications in production, not mock-ups: multilingual AI coaches, a recruiting portal with a privacy model, a training-document generator — designed, secured and deployed.
bia.scope: 💡 The prices shown apply to a micro-organisation — up to 25 employees. Beyond that, scope and the number of teams change the workload: we issue a quote after scoping, using the same method.
bia.vid1_d: We measure the real work, then every task gets a decision: delegate, supervise, or keep human.
bia.vid2_d: One single task taken all the way: written criteria, human control, tests, measurement. The AI never signs.
bia.vid3_d: Month 3: tests replayed, drift caught and fixed, one new use case, the team growing its skills.
bia.vid_d: Three short videos follow a typical case — a 12-person NGO — from the diagnostic to the third month of support. You will see which precise tasks get automated, which stay supervised, and which do not move at all.
bia.vid_note: ⚠️ These are teaching simulations, not results from a real client: the tasks and orders of magnitude are representative of the sector and constitute no quantified promise.

bia.wh2_d: Accounting, insurance, real estate, agencies: writing, client replies, file preparation.
bia.wh3_d: Scheduling, multilingual communication with drivers, compliance tracking.
bia.wh4_d: Administration, communication with families in several languages, lesson preparation.
bia.wh_d: Organisations where the work is real, the means are counted, and trust is essential.

xp.box_h3: What this explorer does — and what it does not
xp.box_p1: It shows the information currently documented by Atmart Data — not everything that exists about a commune. Everything runs in your browser: four public files and one map outline, no application server, no account, no advertising tracker. An anonymous and aggregated audience measurement counts uses (a search happened) without ever knowing who or what — no cookie, no identifier, no IP address kept, and the text you type never leaves your browser: full method. What you see, you can download as is from the catalogue and recompute yourself.
xp.box_p2: The commune is the most detailed territorial level of the public edition. Communal sections, populated places and detailed polygons are available in the Haiti Geo Pack. Definitions, methods and quality statuses are set out on the Backbone page.
xp.class_note: Departments and arrondissements have no values of their own: they are aggregated from their communes according to the rule written in the dictionary, and the number of documented communes is shown alongside. The + button adds a territory to the comparison.
xp.comp_note: Two to four territories side by side — communes, arrondissements or departments. Every value carries its reference year, and comparisons across different years are flagged rather than smoothed over.
xp.desc: Search any commune in Haiti and read its territorial profile: essential services, available indicators, sources and reference years.
xp.kreyol: Find a commune. Read its profile.

xp.lead: Search a commune, an arrondissement or a department, and read its profile: essential services, available indicators, sources and reference years. Compare territories, spot service gaps and export the results for your reports, projects and decisions.
xp.mil_p1: Haiti does not have a single territorial reference set, but several vintages that coexist:
xp.mil_p2: Exact wording: this version of the Explorer covers the 140 communes of the 2018 CNIGS reference set. More recent vintages recognise additional communes. A territory absent from 2018 is not a territory that does not exist — it is absent from that vintage.
xp.mil_p3: For the Ouest department: the 2018 CNIGS reference set contains 20 communes. This number may differ in more recent reference sets. We obtained it by counting this file, not by taking it from a third party.
xp.mil_p4: The vintage correspondence table (CSV, 192 entities) gives, for each territory, its Atmart identifier, its p-code, its vintage, its validity dates and a divergence note. Today it holds only the 2018 vintage: the others will be added when we have the official files, not before.
xp.mil_p5: We do not pick a number in silence: the explorer counts what the reference set it loads actually contains, and names it. Communes created after 2018 will be added with their validity dates as soon as an official reference set publishes them with their codes, without rewriting history. xpl.box.h3: What this explorer does — and what it does not
xpl.box.p1: It shows the information Atmart Data currently documents — not everything that exists about a commune. Everything runs in your browser: three public files, no server, no account, no tracker. What you see, you can download as is from the catalogue and recompute yourself.
xpl.box.p2: The commune is the most detailed territorial level in the public edition. Communal sections, localities and detailed polygons are available in the Haiti Geo Pack. Definitions, methods and quality statuses are set out on the Backbone page.
xpl.comp.intro: Two to four territories side by side — communes, arrondissements or departments. Every value carries its reference year, and comparisons across different reference years are flagged rather than smoothed over.
xpl.hook: Find a commune. See its profile.
xpl.lead: Search for a commune, an arrondissement or a department, and consult its profile: essential services, available indicators, sources and reference years. Compare territories, spot service gaps and export the results for your reports, projects and decisions.
xpl.mill.exact: Exact wording: this version of the Explorer covers the 140 communes of the CNIGS 2018 referential. More recent reference years recognise additional communes. A territory absent from 2018 is not a non-existent territory — it is absent from that reference year.
xpl.mill.intro: Haiti does not have a single territorial referential, but several coexisting reference years:
xpl.mill.li1: 2003 census (IHSI) — the last exhaustive demographic base.
xpl.mill.li2: CNIGS / OCHA COD-AB — the administrative division in force, valid as of 29 November 2018 and republished on 26 January 2026. This is the one this explorer uses, because it is the only one providing official join codes and geometries.
xpl.mill.li3: Recent IHSI population estimates — they include communes created after 2018 and therefore show higher totals.
xpl.mill.ouest: For the Ouest department: the CNIGS 2018 referential contains 20 communes there. This number may differ in more recent referentials. We obtained it by counting this file, not by taking it from a third party.
xpl.mill.silence: We do not pick a figure in silence: the explorer counts what the referential it loads actually contains, and names it. Communes created after 2018 will be integrated with their validity dates as soon as an official referential publishes them with their codes, without rewriting history. How the territory referential is built →
xpl.mill.summary: Why does the number of communes vary between sources?
xpl.mill.table: The reference-year correspondence table (CSV, 192 entities) gives, for each territory, its Atmart identifier, its p-code, its reference year, its validity dates and a divergence note. Today it contains only the 2018 reference year: the others will be added when we have the official files, not before.
